#en: This lonely orbital node hangs where nobody bothers to look anymore, a forgotten cog in an old refinery network still dutifully sampling skies no one thinks to question. That is exactly why her fingerprints would linger here: spliced into legacy routines that kept running long after their operators rotated out, quietly folding her altered readings and storm tracks into every weather model downstream. Pulling the raw telemetry from this vantage is the only way to see which worlds her corrections keep bending toward, without the filters added later to hide them.  \nUp to now the trail has come from a nameless fringe tip, guarded files at a support post, and shipping records in Neon's shadows; together they suggest someone has been riding the same narrow band of routes, letting obsolete systems carry work no one officially remembers authorizing.
zh: 这座孤独的轨道节点悬在再没人费心去看的地方，一台被遗忘的齿轮，仍在一张旧炼油网络里尽职地采样着没人想着去质疑的天空。这正是她的指纹会留在这里的原因：接进那些在操作员轮岗之后仍继续运行的遗留程序，悄悄把她被改动的读数与风暴轨迹折进下游每一个天气模型。从这个视角拉取原始遥测，是看清她的修正不断朝哪些世界弯折的唯一办法——不用后来为了掩盖它们而加的过滤器。  \n目前为止，这条线索来自一条无名的边境线报、某座补给站里戒备的文件，以及霓虹城阴影中的航运记录；合在一起，它们暗示有人一直在同一条狭窄的航线上骑行，让作废的系统承载着没人正式记得批准过的工作。

#en: Out here, where a UC listening post once sifted whispers from the dark, only dead consoles and cold antennae remain, the perfect place to bury something meant to be half-forgotten. The Renegade Guard have taken to using the abandoned arrays as their own filter, catching and trimming any transmission that still dares to speak Catalyst's name, cutting and splicing casualty traffic until no one can say what really happened to the people she treated off the books. What survives is scattered across corrupted logs, half-burned debriefs, and field reports annotated in three different hands, none of them entirely honest. So far, the trail begins with a gutted courier loaded with misrouted chems and continues through a medical station's split routing codes, each fragment pointing toward a medic who keeps rewriting her own story in other people's blood.
zh: 在这里，在一座联殖听音哨曾从黑暗中筛出低语之处，只剩下死掉的控制台与冰冷的天线，是埋葬某种"注定要被半遗忘"之物的完美地点。"叛徒卫队"已习惯于把那些被弃置的阵列当作自己的过滤器，捕捉并剪切任何仍敢说出"催化剂"名字的传输，剪接伤亡播报，直到没人说得出她账外治疗过的人究竟遭遇了什么。存活下来的东西散落在损坏的日志、半烧毁的述职与三种不同笔迹批注的战地报告里，没有一份完全诚实。目前为止，这条线索始于一艘载着错投药剂的被掏空信使船，延续于一座医疗站被拆分的路由代码，每一块碎片都指向一名不断用别人的血重写自己故事的医疗兵。

#en: An abandoned farm is the one place his models were never meant to survive; here, no patrol routes or corporate scanners complicate the lines, only wind across empty plots and the echo of a life that should have been ordinary. Vector has chosen ground like this to run his last calculation, close enough to failing homesteads to hear what his numbers have done, far enough from New Atlantis and Neon that LIST, Argos, and UC analysts can still claim ignorance. Each misaligned landing pad, each stripped hab, has funneled him toward this quiet edge where he can erase the last proof of his manipulated routes or vanish into another statistical anomaly. The pattern behind these deaths is brutally straightforward, yet every dataslate, every hushed testimony from a spacer bar or a back table in the Well has somehow made that simplicity harder to pin down.
zh: 一座废弃农场，是他的模型本绝不该存活下来的地方；在这里，没有巡逻航线或公司扫描仪把线条搞复杂，只有吹过空荡地块的风与一段本该平凡之生的回声。"向量"选了这样的地面来跑他最后一次计算——离失败的农庄足够近、能听见他的数字都干了什么，又离新亚特兰蒂斯城与霓虹城足够远、让独立盟、阿戈斯与联殖分析员仍能声称不知情。每一块错位的停机坪、每一间被剥光的居所，都把他引向这道安静的边缘——在那里，他能抹掉自己操弄航线的最后证据，或消失进又一处统计异常。这些死亡背后的模式粗暴地直白，可每一块数据板、每一句来自太空劫匪酒吧或深井区后桌的低声证词，都莫名地让那种简单更难被钉住。

#en: HM-6310 drifts between beacons with its running lights dead, a Navy hull abandoned to slow tumble and the thin hiss of leaking atmosphere. Whatever was done to its comms was not an accident; relays cut clean, antenna feeds scorched, the kind of work that takes time and access codes, not raiders with bolt-cutters. If there is any trace left of when the ship went quietly dark, it will be in the records still trapped inside these bulkheads, not in the sanitized traffic summaries sitting on some desk in New Atlantis. The way the stories stack up, the blackouts did not start with explosions and screaming but with small adjustments to schedules, slight delays in escorts, a convoy reassigned here, a patrol pulled there, until ships like this ended up alone in the wrong lane at the wrong hour and no one could quite remember who signed which order when.
zh: HM-6310在信标之间漂着，航行灯熄灭，一艘被弃给缓慢翻滚与漏气舱壁细微嘶声的海军船壳。对它通讯所做的一切绝非意外：中继被干净切断、天线馈线被烧灼，那种需要时间和访问码、而不是拿着断线钳的掠夺者干的活。若说这艘船悄悄变黑的确切时刻还有任何痕迹，它就会在这具舱壁里仍被困住的记录中，而不是新亚特兰蒂斯城某张桌子上那些净化过的交通摘要里。故事这样堆叠起来看，那些黑障并非始于爆炸与尖叫，而是始于日程的小改动、护航的轻微延误、一支车队被调到这里、一支巡逻队被抽到那里，直到像这样的船在错误的时间、错误的航道上落单，而没人说得清谁在何时签了哪道命令。

#en: The Deimos yard is where old hulls come to be argued over, both in scrap value and in stories people wish they had not heard. Whatever was spilled at that Vanguard hulk has leeched into the metal here, into the residue pooled in cracked tanks and forgotten drums. The ex-military crew watching over this place walk patrols like they are still on someone else's clock, swapping versions of the same operation under their breath: some say it was a clean strike, others mutter about civilian signatures and doctored logs, but every time someone gets too close to naming names, the conversation drifts back to pay and patrol rotations. So far the trail has run from a lonely rock with a discarded record, to this graveyard of Deimos steel, each step hinting that his route through the wreck fields is tied to whatever truth those soldiers refuse to say out loud.
zh: 火卫二场区，是旧船壳被拿来争论的地方——争论拆解价值，也争论人们但愿自己没听过的故事。在那具先锋队残骸上洒出的东西，已渗进这里的金属，渗进裂开的储罐与被遗忘的油桶里积下的残留。看守这地方的老兵船员巡逻得像仍在按别人的时钟走，低声交换着同一次行动的不同版本：有人说那是一次干净打击，另一些人嘟囔着平民签名与被动过手脚的日志，可每次有人太靠近点名的边缘，谈话就漂回薪水与巡逻轮值。目前为止，线索从一块带着被丢弃记录的孤独岩石，延伸到这片火卫二钢铁的墓地，每一步都暗示他穿越残骸场的路线，与那些士兵拒绝大声说出的真相系在一起。

#en: Whoever set this run up understood how the Settled Systems look past anything wearing Trade Authority colors; a courier like this drifts through customs and crosschecks without anyone asking what rides in its data spine. Out here, with power failing and registry tags flickering, the ship is finally honest about what it became a moving splice node between corporate vaults, UC traffic, and the shadow channels Synapse favors. The hull groans in the quiet, lights stuttering over consoles that once carried routine manifests and now hum with patterns meant to be forgotten, archived in motion so no world ever held them for long. Earlier, the trail began with a burned slate in the dust, then half spoken warnings in Neon's bright center; those hints all pointed to altered records, missing routes, and a single engineering signature threaded through it all.
zh: 布置这条航线的人明白，定居星系会如何无视任何披着贸易管理局颜色的东西；像这样的信使船漂过海关与交叉核查，没人会问它数据脊柱里载着什么。在这里，电力衰竭、登记标签闪烁，这艘船终于诚实地面对自己成了什么：公司金库、联殖交通与"突触"偏爱的阴影信道之间的一个移动接驳节点。船壳在寂静中呻吟，灯光在那些曾承载例行舱单、如今嗡鸣着注定被遗忘之模式的控制台上闪烁——它们在被运动中归档，好让任何世界都无法长期持有。早先，这条线索始于尘土里一块烧毁的数据板，然后是霓虹城明亮中心里半说出口的警告；那些暗示全都指向被改动的记录、失踪的航线，以及贯穿其中一道单一的工程签名。

#en: The orbital node hangs just outside the usual traffic lanes, a quiet watcher that only a shipbreaker or surveyor would think to ask for directions. Its telemetry buffers are cluttered with half corrected coordinates and aborted course updates, the kind of messy trail that forms when different pilots, different contracts, and different lies all tug a route a few degrees off in their own favor. Buried under those minor contradictions is the composite pattern that matters a repeating arc toward the same strip of dead space where his tugs always vanish, a path no one ever meant to reveal so clearly. Up to this point, the search has chased a forgotten dataslate, carved marks in a gutted yard, buried sensor echoes in an old bunker, and a hijacked service line in Gagarin Landing all hinting that his orbit around old wrecks is neither random nor solitary.
zh: 那座轨道节点悬在寻常航道之外，一个安静的观察者，只有拆船工或勘探员才会想到向它问路。它的遥测缓冲区塞满半修正的坐标与中断的航向更新，那种当不同飞行员、不同合同与不同谎言各自把一条航线朝自己有利的方向拽偏几度时形成的凌乱痕迹。埋在这些细微矛盾下的，是那个要紧的复合模式：一段朝同一片他那些拖船总是消失的死寂太空重复弯去的弧线，一条没人曾打算透露得如此清楚的路径。到目前为止，搜寻追过一块被遗忘的数据板、被掏空场区里刻下的标记、一座旧掩体里埋着的传感器回声，以及加加林着陆点一条被劫持的服务线，全都暗示他绕着旧残骸的轨道既非随机、也非独行。

#en: Out on this forgotten pad, the robotics sheds are just shells, walls stripped for scrap and gantries hanging like broken ribs, but the acoustics are perfect for catching what should not be there. The crews working this place are grave-robbers of metal and code both, and they have staked their claim on whatever fragment of the emergency grid washed up here. If anything survived the purge of official logs, if any trace of her hand bled into test rigs or maintenance drones, it will be buried under their haul and their guns. The Claim Jumpers guard it not because they understand it, but because someone paid well to make sure it never leaves this dustbowl intact. So far all anyone really has are pieces: a scorched slate by a dead beacon, rumors of hijacked rescue calls, and a quiet pattern in UC telemetry that keeps circling the same missing architect.
zh: 在这片被遗忘的停机坪上，那些机器人棚屋只是空壳，墙壁被剥去当废料，龙门架像断肋骨一样垂着，可这里的声学特性完美适合捕捉不该存在的东西。在这地方干活的队伍既是金属的盗墓者，也是代码的盗墓者，他们已对冲到这里的任何应急网格碎片宣誓主权。若有什么在官方日志的清除中存活下来，若说她的手有任何痕迹渗进测试设备或维护无人机，它就会埋在他们的收获与枪口之下。抢矿队守着它，不是因为他们懂它，而是因为有人花了大价钱确保它永远不会完好地离开这个尘暴窝。目前为止，所有人真正拥有的都只是碎片：一座死信标旁烧焦的数据板、关于被劫持救援呼叫的传闻，以及联殖遥测里不断绕着同一名失踪设计师打转的安静模式。

#en: This maintenance garage matters because it is where the wrong kind of questions have been asked for too long, and the answers were written into metal instead of reports. Someone has been gutting old tugs and drones here, rebuilding them to run off-pattern, siphoning diagnostics and traffic data through a single buried core no official auditor ever signed off on. The Bloodied Phalanx watch the floor with veteran stillness, the kind you learn in briefing rooms where opinions stop one sentence short of insubordination; they have the look of people who were told once too often that curiosity was a liability. Crates marked for routine refit hide navigation slates and jump sequences, the same signature you first saw on the derelict in orbit and again in altered work logs, all pointing toward a single engineer who turned lane safety into a personal weapon.
zh: 这间维修车库之所以要紧，是因为这里太久以来一直在问错误的问题，而答案被写进了金属而不是报告。有人一直在把旧拖船与无人机掏空、重造来反常运行，把诊断与交通数据通过一个无人正式批准的埋藏核心抽取出去。血染方阵以老兵的沉静看着场地，那种在"意见之差一句就是抗命"的简报室里学来的沉静；他们一副被反复告知"好奇心是负担"的样子。标记为例行翻新的箱子里藏着导航数据板与跃迁序列，正是你第一次在轨道弃船上、然后又在被改动的工作日志里见过的那道签名，全都指向同一名把航道安全变成私人武器的工程师。

#en: The beacon is buried in an asteroid field the charts treat as background noise, a scattering of rock and old test debris where signal reflections knot together into something that only a pilot like her would trust. If she is splicing new corridors off the bones of a weapons range, then this is where the geometry first gets bent, where her numbers and the navy's old scars overlap in ways no official lane will ever admit. Locking onto this transmitter means choosing to believe the uglier version of the story, the one where someone has been stitching shortcuts through places that were never meant for traffic. Up to now, all you have are telemetry fragments from that quiet corporate post and a pirate relay full of half-decoded calls; every retelling of how she flies and what she wants has come secondhand, changing slightly with each mouth that repeats it.
zh: 那座信标埋在一片被星图当作背景噪声的小行星带里，一片散布的岩石与旧测试残骸，信号反射在此打结，变成只有像她那样的飞行员才会信任的东西。若她在从一座武器靶场的骨架上拼接新走廊，那么这里就是几何第一次被掰弯的地方，是她的数字与海军旧伤疤以任何官方航道都不肯承认的方式重叠之处。锁定这台发射机，意味着选择相信这个故事更丑的版本——那个有人一直在把捷径缝进从未打算让交通经过之处的版本。目前为止，你只有来自那座安静公司据点的遥测碎片，以及一座塞满半解码呼叫的走私者中继；关于她如何飞行、想要什么的每一次转述都是二手的，每换一张嘴就稍有变化。

#en: The moonside cargo relay hangs low over bare stone, a hollow bone in orbit, its traffic feeds choked with half-sanitized routes and anonymous handoffs that never appear on official charts. This is where smugglers and brokers reconcile the numbers no one wants audited, where manipulated beacons and missing freight quietly resolve into profit, and where the paths Gravline has been carving through emergency lanes finally take on shape. Buried in its local records is the pattern of his movements, a thread only someone with his training would think to weave through rescue corridors and claim cycles, and someone here clearly started tracing it before going dark midstream. All we have so far is a dead beacon shack on a forgotten rock, corrupted diagnostics from an automated plant, and a set of partial manifests tying his accidents to very deliberate payouts.
zh: 那座卫星侧货运中继低悬在赤裸岩石之上，一根轨道上的空心骨，它的交通数据流塞满半清理的航线与从不现身官方星图的匿名交接。这里正是走私者与掮客核对没人想被审计之数字的地方，是被人动手脚的信标与失踪货运悄悄化作利润的地方，也是"重力线"一直在应急航道上凿出的路径终于成形的地方。埋在它本地记录里的，是他动向的模式——一根只有受过他那种训练的人才会想到穿进救援走廊与索赔周期里的线，而这里有个人显然在追查它、追到一半就消失了。目前为止我们只有：一块被遗忘岩石上一座死掉的信标棚屋、一座自动化工厂里损坏的诊断，以及一组把他的事故与非常刻意的赔付系在一起的部分舱单。

#en: Down here the air tastes of rusted brine and old power surges, the whole underbelly humming like a grav-drive on the edge of misjump. This is where Vector would come to ground his equations, buried under neon and secrecy, splicing himself into forgotten relay trunks while gangs and corporate fixers look the other way. The maze of conduits and flooded service halls gives him proximity to the traffic he has been bending for years, and enough noise to hide the last adjustments he needs to turn Neon's lanes into another "corrected" knot in his invisible map. Freighters diverted at impossible angles, corrupted buoys around distant homesteads, half-erased telemetry from dead UC ships, and a data-runner's quiet confession beneath the city all point the same way: someone has been rewriting routes, and no one wants to admit how long the pattern has been there.
zh: 在这下面，空气尝起来像锈蚀的盐卤与旧日的电力浪涌，整个下腹嗡鸣得像一台正处在错跳边缘的引力引擎。这里正是"向量"会来落地他那些方程的地方——埋在霓虹与隐秘之下，把自己接进被遗忘的中继干线，而帮派与公司掮客都转开视线。导管与淹水服务厅构成的迷宫让他贴近自己多年来一直在掰弯的交通，也有足够噪声藏起他最后几处调整——他需要它们把霓虹城的航道变成他那张隐形地图上又一个"修正过的"结。以不可能角度被改道的货船、遥远农庄周围损坏的浮标、死掉联殖船只的半擦除遥测，以及城市下方一名数据跑腿的安静自白，全都指向同一方向：有人在改写航线，而没人愿意承认这个模式存在了多久。

#en: On the surface this bunker should be dead, just another relic the UC forgot to decommission properly, yet the walls still thrum with low-duty cycles no one logged and antennae still track a sky no one is supposed to be watching. Whatever legacy routines survived here have been quietly repurposed, turning this place into a blind mirror of the patrol grid she once helped design, catching echoes of ships that never appeared on official reports. If those echoes can be read, they will show how she has been slipping through restricted airspace, testing the same gaps her superiors once ordered her to ignore. So far the trail runs from a gutted robotics site rigged for clandestine upgrades to stolen atmospheric scans showing a single signature ghosting through secured lanes, all pointing back toward forgotten UC infrastructure where someone is still listening.
zh: 表面上，这座掩体本该是死的，不过是联殖忘了妥善退役的又一件遗物；可墙壁仍在以无人记录的低温占空比嗡鸣，天线仍在追踪一片没人该监视的天空。在这里幸存的任何遗留程序都被悄悄改作他用，把这地方变成她曾协助设计的那张巡逻网格的一面盲镜，捕捉着从未出现在官方报告里的船只回声。若那些回声能被读取，它们会显示她如何溜过受限空域，测试着她上级曾命令她忽略的同样那些空隙。目前为止，线索从一座被改装用于秘密升级的被掏空机器人场址，延伸到显示单一签名幽灵般穿过安全航道的被盗大气扫描，全都指回被遗忘的联殖基础设施——那里仍有人在聆听。

#en: Down here, beneath Neon's gloss and lightning, signals slip between dripping conduits and rusted catwalks where no official registry bothers to listen. This is where smugglers and failed technicians hide their experiments, where a nav-savant could bury something that talks to Grav Drives without ever tripping a corporate monitor. If there is a device bending lanes around patrol nets, its heartbeat will echo best in this tangle of forgotten relays and jury-rigged boosters, half-maintained by people who swear they saw "ghost jumps" flicker on backroom scanners while others laugh it off as Aurora paranoia. So far the trail has been a half-scrubbed slate on a lonely rock and guarded notes from a research team, all hinting at altered corridors, missing ships, and one vanished contractor whose fingerprints keep surfacing in the margins of other people's data.
zh: 在这下面、在霓虹城的亮面与闪电之下，信号溜进滴水的导管与锈蚀栈道之间，那里的任何官方登记册都懒得去听。这里正是走私者与失败技师藏起实验的地方，是一名导航天才能在不触发公司监控的情况下埋下某个"与引力引擎对话"之物的地方。若说有一台设备在把航道绕巡逻网掰弯，它的心跳会在这团被遗忘中继与临时拼凑升压器的乱麻里回响得最清楚——这些东西由那些发誓在后室扫描仪上见过"幽灵跃迁"闪烁、而另一些人一笑置之说是极光妄想症的人半打理着。目前为止，这条线索是一块孤独岩石上被半擦除的数据板，以及一支研究队伍里戒备的笔记，全都暗示着被改动的走廊、失踪的船只，以及一名消失的承包商——他的指纹不断在别人数据的页边浮现。

#en: The derelict hull drifting ahead once flew under UC colors, its silhouette as familiar to patrol charts as a commuter shuttle, and that is exactly why no one looked too closely when it went dark. A SysDef frame disappearing during a quiet operation is the sort of loss buried in routine, the kind of absence that lets a controller slip experiments into live traffic and blame the void when ships do not arrive. Whatever survived inside this carcass is a record of that comfort, of favors traded and anomalies waved through because the uniforms were the right shade. So far the trail runs from a forgotten dataslate on a remote rock to half-whispered rumors in Neon's upper terraces; now the missing logs and corrupted pings from this lost patrol hint that her hand has been inside military corridors as surely as civilian lanes, and none of them wanted to admit it.
zh: 前方漂着的那具弃船船壳曾挂着联殖的颜色飞行，它的轮廓对巡逻星图来说是通勤穿梭机般熟悉的，而这正是它在变黑时没人仔细看的原因。一具星防队的船架在一次安静行动中失踪，是那种被例行公事埋葬的损失，是那种能让调度员把实验溜进实时交通、并在船只未抵达时归咎于虚空的缺席。这具残骸里存活下来的任何东西，都是那份"安逸"的记录——记录了人情往来与被挥手放行的异常，只因为这些制服颜色对了。目前为止，线索从一块偏远岩石上被遗忘的数据板，延伸到霓虹城上层露台里半低语的传闻；如今，这支失踪巡逻队缺失的日志与损坏的脉冲暗示，她的手既伸进了民用航道，也肯定伸进了军用走廊，而没人愿意承认这一点。

#en: The Ranger outpost is where nervous stories go to be filed away and forgotten, unless someone bothers to read them like a weather map instead of a complaint list. Settlers passing through here talk about strange clouds and broken forecasts only in low voices, as if the wrong adjective might summon more trouble from the sky, and the liaison has been stitching those whispers together into something that looks uncomfortably like a pattern. Buried in those incident notes is the first honest record of where she has passed and how the air changed after she left.  \nSo far all I have is a vague tip from the fringe and a sense that official channels are pretending not to notice; this is the first place where people who actually watched the storms form have tried to put what they saw into words, then lowered their voices and hoped no one important was listening.
zh: 游骑兵前哨，是紧张的故事被归档并遗忘的地方——除非有人费心把它们当作天气图、而不是投诉清单来读。路过的定居者只低声谈论古怪的云与失灵的预报，仿佛用错一个形容词就会从天空招来更多麻烦；而那位联络官一直在把那些低语缝成某种看起来令人不安地像模式的东西。埋在那事件笔记里的，是她曾经过何处、以及她离开后空气如何变化的第一份诚实记录。  \n目前为止，我只有来自边境的一条模糊线报，以及一种官方信道正在假装没注意到的感觉；这是第一次，有真正看着风暴成形的人试图把他们所见写进文字，然后压低声音，希望没有要紧的人在听。

#en: The orbit here is cluttered with old traffic ghosts and discarded buoys, the kind of junk ring no one charts anymore because it is safer to give it wide berth. That is exactly why someone has been using it, stitching subtle course corrections into the noise so passing ships slide into one of two invisible lanes without ever knowing who guided them. The Crimson Fleet hull sitting watch on the edge of this debris is not here for charity; they are guarding a sliver of sky worth killing over, a tool that decides which convoys live, which vanish, and which storms arrive right on time. So far, the trail runs from a frozen lab full of twisted signals to a ranger's hut tracking twin scars in the dust, and now to a derelict Navy run that bent too close to shear, all touched by the same unseen hand before everyone involved drifted away, leaving the pattern behind.
zh: 这里的轨道塞满了旧交通幽灵与被丢弃的浮标，那种再没人测绘的垃圾环——因为它太危险，最好远远绕开。这正是有人一直在利用它的原因：把细微的航向修正缝进噪声里，让过往船只滑进两条隐形航道中的一条，而浑然不知是谁在引导。停在这片残骸边缘警戒的那具深红舰队船壳不是来做慈善的；他们守着一条值得为之杀人的天空缝隙，一件决定哪些车队活、哪些消失、哪些风暴准时抵达的工具。目前为止，线索从一座塞满扭曲信号的冰封实验室，到一座追踪尘土中两道平行伤疤的游骑兵小屋，再到一次弯得离剪切面过近的废弃海军航行，全都在所有相关者飘然离去、只留下模式之前，被同一只无形的手触碰过。

#en: Out here in thin orbit, away from ports and patrol routes, the only witnesses are dead satellites and the faint smear of exhaust on vacuum. This is where someone in a hurry would dump raw navigation work, splice it into an automated relay, and trust that nobody ever looks twice at telemetry meant for dust storms and refinery yield charts. The vectors she has been riding between storm-torn farms, old research shells, and fuel-rich rocks will only line up cleanly from this vantage, where gravity, magnetosphere, and flight paths can be seen in one sweep instead of scattered logs.  \nSo far the trail has run from a nameless backwater tip, to guarded files at a frontier post, to strange readings along a Helium-3 line, then into Neon's underlevel wiring and an abandoned raider chart; each step tighter, each rushed decision leaving a small, crooked mark behind.
zh: 在这里的稀薄轨道上，远离港口与巡逻航线，唯一的证人是死掉的卫星与真空上那抹淡淡的废气痕。这里正是一个匆忙的人会倾倒原始导航工作、把它接进自动化中继，并笃信没人会多看一眼那些本为沙尘暴与炼油产量图表准备的遥测的地方。她一直在风暴摧残的农场、旧研究空壳与富燃料岩石之间骑行的向量，只有从这个视角才能整齐对齐——在这里，引力、磁层与飞行路径能一次扫清，而不是散落在日志里。  \n目前为止，线索从一条无名穷乡线报，到某座边境哨所里戒备的文件，再到氦-3 航线沿线的古怪读数，然后钻进霓虹城下层的线路与一张废弃掠夺者星图；每一步都更紧，每一个匆忙的决定都留下一道小小的歪斜记号。

#en: Out here the sky is empty and the ground is nothing but scrub and wind, the kind of place freight captains and smugglers both use when they want their paperwork to quietly slip between jurisdictions. Whatever list was compiled here, it would have been built from a dozen minor favors and half-heard instructions, a route stitched together by dispatchers who misread storm warnings, handlers who rounded up coordinates, and pilots who logged their cargo under the wrong codes on purpose. That is why this backwater matters: it is where the little errors and quiet lies converge into a clear pattern of ships moving under engineered weather. So far the trail has run from a lonely stash in the dirt, to a bounty-hunter hulk with half its records burned out, to a derelict orbiting grid and a rusting company town whose harvests refuse to match their own climate models.
zh: 在这里，天空空空荡荡，地面只有灌木与风，货运船长与走私者想让自己文书悄悄在管辖缝隙间滑过时都会用的那种地方。无论在这里编成的是一份什么清单，它都会是由十几个小人情与半听来的指令搭成的航线，由误读风暴警告的调度员、把坐标凑整的经手人，以及故意用错误代码登记货物的飞行员缝在一起。正因如此，这片穷乡才要紧：正是在这里，小小的错误与安静的谎言汇聚成一种清晰的模式——船只在人造天气下行进。目前为止，线索从尘土中一处孤独的藏匿点，到一具记录被烧毁一半的赏金猎人残骸，再到一座废弃的轨道网格与一座丰收拒绝与自身气候模型相符的锈蚀公司镇。
